claim: "Students must register prior to the beginning of classes in the fall. Students who cannot attend the scheduled fall-term registration must receive written permission from their program chair and notify the registrar in advance. All international students are required to complete a nonacademic registration with the Office of International Students and Scholars prior to the beginning of classes, in addition to the School's registration." Also: "All students must submit their course schedules to the registrar within one week of the first day of classes of each term"
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.144
supports: registration is a pre-classes step; missing it requires chair's written permission
uncertainty: No online-registration mechanics, late-registration fee, or explicit consequence of missing registration is stated in the DGSD bulletin (searched: not found).
suggestedSimplification: Model registration as a one-time action in the Aug 24-29 window; missing it without permission blocks the term.

claim: "A student who does not apply for a personal leave of absence, or who applies for a leave but is not granted one, and who does not register for any term, is considered to have withdrawn from the School."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.159 (Personal Leave of Absence)
supports: non-registration for a term = withdrawal
suggestedSimplification: Not registering for a term => withdrawn.

claim: Financial hold: "The Office of Student Accounts will impose late fees of $125 per month (up to a total of $375 per term) if any part of the term bill ... is not paid when due. ... While on Financial Hold, the university will not provide diplomas and reserves the right to withhold registration or withdraw the student for financial reasons."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.184
appliesTo: all students with unpaid term charges
supports: late fee is for unpaid bills, not late registration
uncertainty: This is a billing late fee, not a late-registration fee. No DGSD late-registration fee found.
suggestedSimplification: Unpaid bill: $125/month up to $375/term; hold blocks diploma.

claim: 2026-27 calendar: Aug 17-21 "Required pre-orientation training and workshops as scheduled (including but not limited to International Student Orientation, Design Tutorials, and Playwriting Hansberry Welcome)"; Aug 24 "Fall term time begins"; Aug 24-29 "Required training and orientation sessions for first-year students as scheduled"; Aug 26-29 "Required training and orientation sessions for returning students as scheduled"; Aug 31 "Fall term classes begin, 9:00am"; Sept 7 Labor Day.
source: DGSD Academic Calendar 2026-27 web page; Bulletin calendar p.5 (PDF column layout garbled; consistent reading: Aug 24 term begins + registration, Aug 24-29 required training and orientation, Aug 31 classes begin)
supports: orientation is required, Aug 24-29 for first-years
uncertainty: Content of the orientation sessions (compliance trainings, safety, anti-racism) is not published on public pages; dgsdinfo.yale.edu new-student pages require Yale login. Consequence of missing orientation: not found.
suggestedSimplification: One required 'Orientation week' event Aug 24-29; Acting first-years have no pre-orientation (Aug 17-21) unless international.

claim: "All new students are required to complete these requirements by August 1, 2026 ... All requirements are to be completed through Health On Track". Required for all students: MMR (2 doses), varicella, meningitis ACWY ("only for students residing in university housing"), Tdap within past 10 years, TB screening questionnaire.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.176-177 (Required Immunizations)
supports: health requirements precede orientation (deadline Aug 1, 2026)
uncertainty: Consequence of non-compliance (e.g. registration hold) not stated in bulletin.
suggestedSimplification: Pre-arrival 'health requirements' checklist due Aug 1.

claim: Work-study conversion excludes "Work-study hours missed from an absence, tardiness, delay of I-9 completion, or conflict resolution outside of the prioritized list".
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.147 and p.189
supports: I-9 delay costs unconvertible work-study hours
uncertainty: Bulletin gives no I-9 deadline. Yale Student Jobs: Section 1 via Equifax email link, then "you must visit the I-9 Center in person to complete Section 2" (https://www.yalestudentjobs.org/Cmx_Content.aspx?cpid=33). Deadline/penalty on that page: not found.
suggestedSimplification: If I-9 not done, early work-study hours are lost (not converted to grant).

claim: OISS: F-1/J-1 students may work on campus "up to 20 hours a week when classes are in session", but Yale policy: "students may not work more than 19 hours (combined for all jobs) in any week during the academic term"; full-time during breaks. Departments "should make sure the student has or has applied for a U.S. social security number and completes the I-9 form." Non-Yale J-1 sponsors must give permission first.
source: Yale OISS, Hiring Student Visa Holders
supports: international students can do work-study on campus subject to 19 hr/week cap
uncertainty: Whether DGSD work-study ever approaches 19 hr/week not stated.
suggestedSimplification: International: I-9 + SSN application needed; 19 hr/week cap in term.

claim: DRAM 50a, The Theatrical Event: "In this three-week laboratory introduction, students function as both artists and audience, creating short pieces in response to prompts ... Required of actors, directors, dramaturgs, playwrights, and projection designers during their first term in residence."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.65 (Directing); listed in Acting Year One p.24
supports: DRAM 50 is a required course (Pass/Fail by default), not a production call
uncertainty: No separate attendance threshold; general attendance policy applies.
suggestedSimplification: Required first-term 3-week course.

claim: DRAM 51a/b, New Play Lab: "First-year actors, directors, dramaturgs, and playwrights form three small companies and workshop that play." Acting plan lists DRAM 51b (spring).
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.99 (Playwriting) and p.24 (Acting Year One)
supports: New Play Lab is a required course, not a casting assignment
uncertainty: Description is terse; scheduling (rehearsal-style calls vs class hours) not stated.
suggestedSimplification: Required first-year spring course.

claim: DRAM 363a, You Are the Creator: actors develop individual performance pieces during fall of third year, "a performance that they ultimately share with the Acting Program community at the beginning of the second semester."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.31
appliesTo: third-year Acting, fall course; showing at start of spring
supports: the showing is the culmination of a required fall course
uncertainty: Whether the showing is graded separately: not found.
suggestedSimplification: Third-year fall course whose showing happens in January.

claim: "regular and on-time attendance at scheduled classes, production assignments, rehearsals, work-study assignments, required workshops, and School meetings is both expected and required. Unexcused absences and/or persistent unexcused lateness are behaviors subject to disciplinary action." Calls: "Rehearsal and performance calls are posted each day. Anticipated lateness for these calls must be reported to the individual in charge as soon as possible, but no later than thirty minutes before the call." Disciplinary list includes "recurring lateness and/or unexcused absences from required School/YRT classes, rehearsals, performances, and work calls" (p.155).
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.149, 155
supports: one attendance policy covers classes and calls alike
suggestedSimplification: One attendance rule; lateness to calls must be reported >=30 min ahead.

claim: "The casting pool for School productions and projects consists of those acting students who have demonstrated proficiency in collaboration, professional discipline, and reliability. A student's inability to maintain or apply these practices in class, project, or production circumstances may result in the removal of that actor from the casting pool in order to provide them with an opportunity to reacquire, strengthen, or expand these skills. Once cast in a role, the student is required to fulfill that casting obligation."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.146 (Casting)
supports: removal from casting pool is discretionary, triggered by unreliability in class/project/production
uncertainty: No number of absences is specified (not found). Decision maker implied to be Acting chair (casting assigned by chair, approved by dean).
suggestedSimplification: Chair judgement: repeated unreliability can remove a student from the casting pool; no fixed count.

claim: "All casting of student actors in productions at the School or at Yale Repertory Theatre, including understudy casting, is assigned by the chair of Acting and approved by the dean". Understudies: "Failure to be available to perform as an understudy is treated as a grave breach of professionalism and may be grounds for dismissal."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.146
supports: casting is assigned, not auditioned; understudy no-show can be dismissal
suggestedSimplification: Chair assigns roles; missed understudy call = possible dismissal.

claim: Declining/withdrawing from an assignment needs chair and assistant dean approval and "may negatively affect the student's progress toward a degree"; "The School also reserves the right to remove any student from a production assignment for persistent or egregious unprofessionalism. Students removed from assignments are not guaranteed replacement assignments". "All students with program assignments on School productions and projects are obligated to strike the show and are assigned work-study for that call."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.145
supports: assignments are obligations; strike is paid work-study
suggestedSimplification: Removal from a production is possible; strike counts as work-study.

claim: "Rehearsals are normally scheduled from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m., Tuesday through Friday, with earlier start times possible on Saturdays and during technical rehearsals. Sunday is normally the day off." Max six hours/day for a major School production; "Actors who are double cast are ordinarily not called more than six hours a day and cannot participate in Yale Cabaret productions."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.146-147
supports: rehearsal hours and double-casting cap
suggestedSimplification: Rehearsal block Tue-Sat 3-10pm, <=6h/day.

claim: Acting program: "attendance at all scheduled classes, tutorials, conferences, rehearsal calls, work-study assignments, production assignments, and all School productions is expected and mandatory. If students are unable to be in attendance as expected due to personal illness or family emergency, they have a responsibility to notify all those who will be affected by their absence and in as timely a manner as possible."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.24
supports: Acting students must also attend all School productions
suggestedSimplification: Illness: notify everyone affected promptly.

claim: "Students whose health needs, including medical appointments, require them to miss or be late for class should alert their professors by email, copying their program's chair and senior administrative assistant. Students remain responsible for the work missed, on a schedule determined by the professor."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.149
supports: illness absence = notify by email; makeup on professor's schedule
uncertainty: No documentation (doctor's note) requirement stated for short illness: not found.
suggestedSimplification: Illness: email professors + chair; makeup work set by professor.

claim: Multi-class/work-study absences must be requested in advance via the electronic absence request form at your.drama.yale.edu; "Requests for absences that would interfere with existing academic work or required work-study obligations will not be approved unless alternate arrangements are possible. If work-study clearance is granted, then the program chair will determine whether or not to approve the absence. Workstudy hours missed during a planned absence are not eligible for conversion."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.149
supports: planned absence needs work-study clearance then chair approval
suggestedSimplification: Planned absence request: labor supervisor then chair.

claim: Immediate family death: "three consecutive weekdays of excused absences, without penalty"; on return "they must submit to the assistant dean an obituary notice, a funeral or memorial program, or other documentation"; "the student remains responsible for missed academic work." Emergency grant may cover travel.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.150
supports: documented 3-day excused absence
suggestedSimplification: 3 excused weekdays; documentation after return.

claim: Five work periods per year during which classes are suspended; "all students are expected to be in attendance"; absence request required to be away.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.150
supports: work periods are term time
suggestedSimplification: Treat work periods as required presence.

claim: Three types: personal, medical, parental. Approved by program chair and dean (medical also needs Yale Health physician recommendation). Leave of "one, two, or three terms"; on leave: no degree requirements except extended coursework; "not eligible for financial aid, including loans"; no university facilities; not eligible for Yale Health Basic or Hospitalization/Specialty coverage: "Coverage terminates the day the leave is granted"; DGSD "will cover the cost of Yale Health Affiliate Coverage for students on medical leave, for up to three terms"; return: notify registrar in writing "at least eight weeks prior to the end of the approved leave"; not returning without extension => "automatically dismissed from the School."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.157-158
supports: leave suspends aid and health coverage; failure to return = dismissal
suggestedSimplification: Leave: 1-3 terms; no aid; health via affiliate plan (school pays if medical); no-show at end = dismissed.

claim: Eligible "after satisfactory completion of at least one term of study. Personal leaves cannot be granted retroactively, and normally are not approved after the tenth day of a term." Must be current with degree requirements.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.158
supports: personal leave unavailable in first term and after day 10
suggestedSimplification: Personal leave only from term 2, before day 10.

claim: Medical leave on written recommendation of a Yale Health physician, any time after matriculation if making satisfactory progress; mandatory medical leave possible on Yale Health recommendation (appeal within seven days); "A student who is placed on medical leave during any term has tuition adjusted according to the same schedule used for withdrawals"; return requires "written permission to return from a physician at Yale Health."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.159
supports: medical leave requires Yale Health sign-off both ways
suggestedSimplification: Medical leave: Yale Health note out and back.

claim: Withdrawal: submit withdrawal form to registrar; "Normally, a student or intern who has chosen to withdraw is eligible to apply for readmission. A student or intern who is asked to withdraw by the faculty or is dismissed by the School is not eligible to apply for readmission." Dismissal: "Once dismissed, a student is not eligible for readmission." Leave: no readmission application needed, just written notice 8 weeks before end.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.157, 160
supports: voluntary withdrawal allows reapplication; dismissal and asked-to-withdraw do not; leave returns without application
uncertainty: Readmission process details for withdrawn students: not found.
suggestedSimplification: Leave = return guaranteed; Withdraw = may reapply; Dismissed = never.

claim: Notice of academic concern is informal; "If the academic concern is not remediated within one semester, the issue may be escalated to formal academic warning." Warning is a formal meeting; written letter sets "the improvement required within a defined time frame"; "Institutional and federal aid for students on academic warning will be unaffected during their remediation period(s). Students on academic warning may not participate in the Yale Cabaret." "Failure to remediate the academic warning within the defined time frame may lead to dismissal."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.154
supports: concern -> warning -> possible dismissal; aid unaffected
uncertainty: No fixed length of the warning period.
suggestedSimplification: Concern (1 semester to fix) -> Warning (deadline in letter) -> Dismissal.

claim: Students not meeting standards "may be dismissed, whether or not they are on academic warning." "Serious breaches ... or serious negligence in work-study assignments may lead to immediate dismissal of a student who is not currently on academic warning." Students may be warned or dismissed "at any time despite having achieved passing grades in all coursework." Disciplinary panel: dismissal recommendation requires unanimous vote.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.151, 156, 157
supports: dismissal is faculty/dean judgement independent of grades
suggestedSimplification: Dismissal possible without warning for serious breach.

claim: "approval from the chairs of the following academic programs is required in advance before a student commits to participation in the Yale Cabaret: Directing and Acting. ... No student on academic warning in any program may participate in the cabaret." Conflicts with priorities "will not be resolved in favor of the cabaret"; failure to avoid conflicts "may result in academic warning or dismissal."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.148
supports: Cabaret needs Acting chair pre-approval; warning bars participation; Cabaret ranks 6th of 7 priorities
uncertainty: Whether eligibility is rechecked mid-production if a student goes on warning: not stated (not found). Reading 'may not participate' literally implies withdrawal from an ongoing show, but that is an inference.
suggestedSimplification: Gate Cabaret on chair approval + not on warning; drop from show if warning issued (inference).

claim: Acting chapter: "The program's chair works directly with the Yale Cabaret artistic directors regarding approval of Cabaret participation by actors. Participation in Yale Cabaret productions is dependent on students' program-related casting obligations and academic standing."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.24
supports: casting obligations and standing gate Cabaret
suggestedSimplification: Same as above.

claim: Priority order for conflicts: 1 Yale Rep calls; 2 DGSD classes; 3 ticketed School productions; 4 other assigned projects; 5 required work-study; 6 "Yale Cabaret productions, which are extracurricular"; 7 approved outside work/affinity events/elective work-study.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.142
supports: Cabaret loses every conflict except outside work
suggestedSimplification: Use as conflict-resolution ladder.

claim: DGSD website (older wording): "No student with an incomplete and no second- or third-year student on probation may participate in the Yale Cabaret in any capacity."
source: drama.yale.edu Production Opportunities page
supports: Incomplete also bars Cabaret (website)
uncertainty: Conflicts with 2026-27 Bulletin, which for Acting/general policy says only 'academic warning' (the Incomplete bar appears in the Bulletin for TD&P, Dramaturgy and technical interns). Bulletin is authoritative.
suggestedSimplification: Use Bulletin rule (warning bars) for actors.

claim: "Actors who are double cast are ordinarily not called more than six hours a day and cannot participate in Yale Cabaret productions."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.147
supports: double-cast actors barred from Cabaret
suggestedSimplification: Double-cast => no Cabaret.

claim: "During the summer, Yale Summer Cabaret is the exploratory theatrical home for David Geffen School of Drama students. Like Yale Cabaret, it is student-run and interdisciplinary. Each season, a new artistic and management team has the opportunity to shape the theater's vision".
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.141
supports: Summer Cabaret is student-run, summer
uncertainty: Eligibility rules, pay/stipend amount, and whether graduating students may join: not found in Bulletin, summercabaret.org, or yalecabaret.org.
suggestedSimplification: Summer Cabaret open to continuing students; treat pay as unknown/not modelled.

claim: 2026 season ('Spectra') led by co-artistic directors Alex Vasquez Dheming (Lighting MFA), Nate Britton (second-year Projection MFA) and Bobby Marcus; opened June 26, 2026 at 217 Park St.; cast included Ameya Narkar, "a third year actor at the School of Drama" (i.e., rising third-year). 2025 season was co-directed by playwrights "going into their third and final year".
source: summercabaret.org Meet the Team; New Haven Arts Paper
supports: company and leadership drawn from rising 2nd/3rd-years
uncertainty: No evidence either way on graduates; pay not mentioned.
suggestedSimplification: Summer Cabaret for rising 2nd/3rd years only.

claim: Students required to work during a recess ("including summer recess") on a School/Yale Rep production or PWA are "eligible to be paid up to eight hours of recess pay for each recess day" at "the prevailing hourly work-study rate."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.150-151
supports: summer work on assignments is paid at work-study rate
uncertainty: Does not say Summer Cabaret (extracurricular) counts; probably not.
suggestedSimplification: Summer Cabaret pay: not modelled.

claim: Acting plan of study: Year One DRAM 4b, 50a, 51b, 53a, 103a/b, 113a/b, 123a/b, 133a/b, 143a/b, 153a, 163b, 180a, 403a/b, 533a/b, 563a, 863b, 873a/b; Year Two DRAM 163a, 203a/b, 213a/b, 223a/b, 233a/b, 243a/b, 263a/b, 273a, 293b, 353a, 405a/b, 413a/b, 533a/b; Year Three DRAM 190a, 253a, 273b, 303a, 313a/b, 323a/b, 343a/b, 363a, 373a, 423a/b, 463a/b, 473b, 533a/b, 743b, 793b (Actor Showcase); plus casting assignments each year (Yale Rep understudy from 2nd semester of year one).
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.24-25
supports: required sequence of courses + assignments
suggestedSimplification: Model per-year course list.

claim: Additional degree requirements: DRAM 863b Principles of Anti-Racist Theater (anti-racist requirement); DRAM 873a/b Text and Context (theater history); CRP (DRAM 4b): "Failure to successfully complete CRP will prevent students from meeting the requirements for graduation." Anti-racist: "Failure to attend each program's anti-racist theater practice requirement will prevent students from meeting the requirements for graduation."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.25-26, 144-145
supports: three named non-negotiable requirements
suggestedSimplification: Three flag requirements: CRP, anti-racism, theater history.

claim: "Except where noted, courses at the School are offered on a Pass/Fail basis." Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail scales apply only to Stage Management, TD&P (at instructor discretion) and Dramaturgy.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.151-152
supports: Acting courses are Pass/Fail
suggestedSimplification: Pass/Fail only.

claim: "Should a student fail to complete all required coursework by the end of a term, a student may request a grade of Incomplete. If granted by the instructor, the student is required to complete the remaining coursework within one month of the end of the term. ... may petition the instructor for an extension. If ... the course requirements are not met, the grade of Incomplete will be converted to a grade of Permanent Incomplete which does not confer credit." Financial aid section: "Grades of Incomplete, or petitions for extension, must be resolved by registration day of the following term."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.152, 195
supports: Incomplete: 1 month, extendable; else Permanent Incomplete (no credit)
uncertainty: Two deadlines (one month vs next registration day) coexist; the latter is for SAP/aid purposes.
suggestedSimplification: Incomplete resolves within 1 month or becomes no-credit.

claim: "In order to be eligible for participation in the Actor Showcase and to participate in Commencement ceremonies, any acting student carrying an outstanding Incomplete grade in any coursework must satisfy the course requirements by the fourth week of their final semester and before course DRAM 793b, Actor Showcase, begins."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.26
supports: outstanding Incomplete by week 4 of final term bars Showcase and Commencement
uncertainty: Does not say the degree is withheld permanently, only participation.
suggestedSimplification: Clear incompletes by week 4 of final spring or lose Showcase/Commencement.

claim: "Students who have satisfactorily completed their course of study and have successfully fulfilled all nonclassroom requirements of their program are recommended by a majority vote of the faculty to receive the Certificate in Drama, M.F.A., or D.F.A., conferred by the president and fellows of Yale University."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.151
supports: faculty majority vote recommends degree
uncertainty: Whether a student on academic warning can graduate: not stated (not found). Nonclassroom requirements not enumerated beyond assignments/work-study/CRP etc.
suggestedSimplification: Degree = all courses passed + nonclassroom requirements + faculty vote.

claim: "For the M.F.A. program, students must complete the degree requirements within nine semesters. Any approved leave of absence cannot exceed three semesters." Traditional time frame six semesters; tuition scholarship "ordinarily limited to six terms of study for M.F.A./certificate programs".
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.194, 182, 190
supports: 9-semester cap; tuition covered for 6 terms
uncertainty: Process for conferring the degree after the third year (e.g., late completion): not found.
suggestedSimplification: Degree must finish within 9 semesters; terms beyond 6 not tuition-covered.

claim: "All candidates on whom degrees or certificates are to be conferred must be present at the Commencement exercises unless excused for urgent reasons by their program chair with the approval of the dean. Requests to be excused from Commencement must be submitted by April 30, 2027." University Commencement May 24, 2027.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.162; calendar p.5
supports: attendance at Commencement required
suggestedSimplification: Commencement May 24, 2027.

claim: "Students may be disqualified and may not be allowed to continue at the School if they receive (1) two Failures in any one semester; (2) a total of three Failures by the end of the second term; (3) Failure in four or more courses by the end of the third term; (4) ... five ... by the end of the fourth term; (5) ... six ... by the end of the fifth term; (6) Failure in a total of seven or more courses." Pace: complete at least 75% of attempted credits.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.194
supports: failure counts that can trigger disqualification
suggestedSimplification: Fail counts threshold for dismissal risk.

claim: "For the 2026-2027 year, we expect all students and interns will work a minimum of 200 work-study hours, 150 assigned and 50 elective." "Failure to complete assigned work-study, outside of excused absences, is considered a breach of professionalism and may lead to academic warning or dismissal."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.147
supports: 200 hrs (150 assigned + 50 elective); shortfall is a professionalism issue
uncertainty: Financial aid chapter (p.189) frames the 50 elective as optional: "We anticipate that students can also find an additional fifty hours or more of elective work-study, if they choose."
suggestedSimplification: 150 assigned mandatory; 50 elective optional income.

claim: "in the 2026-27 academic year, these jobs are compensated at the rate of $23 per hour"; "Work-study earnings are paid when worked". Bulletin: "Work-study earnings are paid weekly or semi-monthly."
source: DGSD Financial Aid page; DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.189
supports: $23/hr in 2026-27 ($22 in 2025-26 per search summary)
suggestedSimplification: $23/hr, paid as worked.

claim: If the School can't assign the full 150 hours, or a student on aid falls short due to School/Yale Rep conflicts or approved extenuating circumstances "such as illness or injury", unearned hours (up to 150) can be converted to grant-in-aid; "Conversions are processed in January and May". Not convertible: absence, tardiness, I-9 delay, out-of-priority conflict, planned absences, outside work, outside classes.
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.147, 189
supports: illness-missed hours can be made whole; other misses are lost money
suggestedSimplification: Illness shortfall -> grant; other shortfall -> lost wages.

claim: "For all separations, guaranteed work-study funding will not be refunded to a student for hours not worked."
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) p.183
supports: no payout for unworked hours on separation
suggestedSimplification: Leaving forfeits remaining work-study.

claim: Basic Student Health Services: free, automatic; new students from "the date the student is required to be on campus for orientation and continue through July 31". Hospitalization & Specialty Care: auto-enrolled and billed each term; new students covered from dorm opening/orientation; continuing: fall-only Aug 1-Jan 31, spring-only Feb 1-Jul 31; waiver deadline Sept 15 (full year/fall) or Jan 31 (spring).
source: DGSD Bulletin 2026-2027 (Bulletin of Yale University Series 122 No. 14, Aug 30, 2026) pp.171-173
supports: coverage periods
suggestedSimplification: Coverage from orientation day through July 31.
